fatal_errors: The hypothesis never identifies the specific candidate interlayer compositions CrFeTaVW and CrFeTiVW.

It replaces the target study's comparison of Ta- and Ti-containing RHEAs, hybrid MD/MC simulations, mechanical alloying, SPS consolidation, and thermal-diffusivity characterization with an unreported diffusion-bonding study.

The claimed mitigation of thermal-expansion mismatch, suppression of interdiffusion, and prevention of brittle phases was not established by the target study; CrFeTaVW actually formed an Fe2Ta C14 Laves phase.
The cited evidence only supports general high-temperature or irradiation promise of RHEAs and does not validate performance as a W/CuCrZr interlayer.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad application of a refractory high-entropy alloy between W and CuCrZr, but it does not reconstruct the material or evidence in the target paper. The relevant candidates are equiatomic CrFeTaVW and CrFeTiVW, selected because their multielement disorder produces low thermal diffusivity relative to W and CuCrZr, while retaining predominantly bcc-derived structures after mechanical alloying and SPS. Ta-to-Ti substitution changes phase constitution but has little effect on diffusivity. The generated mechanism instead centers on an intermediate thermal-expansion coefficient and diffusion-barrier behavior, neither of which was measured or demonstrated. Its proposed controlled W/CuCrZr joint experiment is reasonably discriminating as future work, but the conditions are vague and the evidence supplied cannot support its central claims.
